issues.where: whole beat 3 (paint), also set-A-07 to set-A-09 and set-B-07 to set-B-09
issues.what: 6 s on a bare bonnet curve. There is no feature line, badge, edge or readable background, so nothing tells you what you are looking at. In the tall frames 60 to 70% of the frame is blank panel, and the end frames (set-A-09, set-B-09) are close to a flat gray field. Lighting will not make this framing work.
issues.fix: Frame on a character line, such as the shoulder crease running into the DRL or a door blade. Keep a strip of readable background, track along the line so the highlight has something to travel over, and compose the tall version on a vertical feature instead of center-cropping the wide.

issues.where: beats 1, 2 and 8 (set-C-01, set-C-02, set-C-08, set-A-01 to set-A-06, set-A-22 to set-A-24)
issues.what: About 22 of the 45 s use one setup: low front three-quarter at knee height, centered, slow push in or pull out. The cut from beat 1 to 2 at 4.00 s (set-A-03 to set-A-04) barely changes the frame, and beat 8 is beats 1 and 2 played backwards. The ignition wide in beat 7 sits at the same low height, so the film never leaves knee height.
issues.fix: Give beat 2 (wake) its own setup, for example a low profile track or a high three-quarter looking down onto the DRL. Put at least one wide at a clearly different height (high or overhead), so beat 8's pull-out reads as a return and not a repeat.

issues.what: In the tall lamp frames the apex of the Y-shaped DRL is cut by the right edge, and the push slides it further out of frame. By set-B-15 only the projector lens and a sliver of light bar are left, so the signature lamp is lost in the format where it should fill the height.
issues.fix: Reframe the tall camera to keep the DRL apex inside the frame and compose along the vertical arm of the Y. Aim the push at the apex, not at the projector.

issues.where: lower third, also set-B-01 to set-B-06, set-B-19 to set-B-23
issues.what: The tall wide frames keep the car small, about 15% of frame height, with the bottom 30 to 35% empty floor and nothing in the foreground. They read as a portrait crop of a wide setup, not a framing built for vertical.
issues.fix: Use a longer lens or move closer so the car fills the frame width. Sit it on the lower-third line with the towers above it, and add a foreground cue (lane marking, curb, drain) to carry the bottom of the frame.

issues.where: center, middle of beat 6 (detail), also set-B-16, set-B-17, set-C-06 frames 5 to 8
issues.what: The move through the engine bay passes through soft, overlapping louvres and pipes with no clear subject. The tall version opens on a blurred mass (set-B-16), and only the end frame (set-A-18, set-B-18) lands on a readable V-brace.
issues.fix: Shorten the traverse and settle on the V-brace by mid-beat, or open on one readable louvre edge and rack to the brace. Plan the tall camera so the brace fills its height from the start of the beat.

issues.what: Paint, wheel, lamp and detail are four close or macro beats in a row (about 20 s) with no wide reset. Their lens choices all sit near the same tight field, so the middle of the film loses the sense of where we are on the car.
issues.fix: Vary the focal length across these beats. Make the wheel beat a wider low profile that shows the car's length, or put a short medium shot between the lamp and detail beats.

issues.where: top and left, set-B-10 to set-B-12
issues.what: The tall wheel framing crops away the headlamp and front overhang that anchor the wide version (set-A-10 to set-A-12). You are left with a centered wheel over empty floor and dark background, with no sense of direction.
issues.fix: Tilt up a little and offset the wheel low in frame so the fender arch and front corner give the frame a leading line.

issues.what: At the start of the tall ignition beat the car sits hard left, with the front fender and mirror clipped by the frame edge. It only drifts to center later.
issues.fix: Start the tall camera centered on the rear, or offset it so the clipped side has clear breathing room.
